Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 118 s. 2022 October 10, 2022 HON. CHARLOTTE D. PANAL Mayor Municipality of Tambulig Zamboange del Sur Dear Mayor Panal: This has reference to your letter dated August 15, 2022 requesting the Department's opinion on the following issues: I. Is an order for preventive suspension issued by the proper Sangguniang Bayan appealable? Which office has jurisdiction to pass upon an appeal? 2. While it is not stipulated in Rule XIX Disciplinary Action of the Local Government Code, could the Sangguniang Panlalawigan issue a stay of the execution order of a preventive suspension or order the reinstatement of the appellant ex-parte: 3. Given that in the law, upon expiration of the preventive suspension, the suspended elective official is deemed reinstated in the office, which office has the duty to implement a stay or reinstatement order? Båsed on the document forwarded to the Central Office, the foregoing issues were premised on the following facts: An administrative complaint dated May 15, 2022 was filed before the Sangguniang Bayan of the Municipality of Tambulig by six (6) Sangguniang Barangay Members, namely, Eduardo Bocala, Evelyn A. Autida, Flordeliza A. bate, jonafer C. Gomabon, Johana C. Lingolingo and Christopher P. Comonsaid against their Punong Barangay Cecile R Villafuerte of Barangay Cabgan for Grave Misconduct and Dishonesty; Thereafter, the Sangguniang Bayan adopted on June 27, 2022 its Resolution No. 2022-493 recommending for the preventive suspension of Punong Barangay Cecile R. Villafuerte for a period of two (2) months; • On June 28, 2022, you issued a notice of 60-day preventive suspension to PB Villafuerte and ordered the first-ranking sangguniang barangay member to assume as Acting Punong Barangay; "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

PB Villafuerte filed a Memorandum of Appeal before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on July 8, 2022 assailing SB Resolution No. 22-20-493 which recommended her preventive suspension; Thereafter, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability without having received a copy of the assailed SB Resolution and relying only on the implied factual allegations decided ex parte on the Memorandum of Appeal filed by PB Villafuerte. For this,. the Sangguniang Panlalawigan adopted on July 21, 2022 SP Resolution No. 019- 2022 entitled "ADOPTING THE RECOMMENDATION (STAY OF EXECUTION OR ORDER OF REINSTATEMENT) DATED 20 JULY 2022 OF THE COMMITTEE ON GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY RELATIVE TO THE MEMORANDUM OF APPEAL DATED 8 JULY 2022 FILED BY RESPONDENT-APPELLANT PUNONG BARANGAY CECILE R. VILLAFUERTE AGAINST RESPONDENT- APPELLEES EDUARDO BOCALA, EVELYN A. AUTIDA, FLORDELIZA A. BATE, JONAFER C. GOMABON, JOHANA C. LINGOLINGO AND CHRISTOPHER P. COMONSAD, DOCKETED AS ADMINISTRATIVE APPEAL NO. SP-02-2022, THEREBY STAYING THE IMPLEMENTTION OF THE PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION ORDER AGAINST PUNONG BARANGA Y CECILE R. VILLAFUERTE AND LIKEWISE ORDERING HER IMMEDIATE REINSTATEMENT TO HER OFFICE, IF A PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION ORDER WAS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. " • Hence, your request for legal opinion. Since the first and second issues are interrelated, we deem it proper to answer them in one (1) discussion. In this regard, let us examine the provisions of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 pertinent to the case at hand, to wit: a) Section 63, which governs the imposition of preventive suspension "SECTION 63. Preventive Suspension. (a) Preventive suspension may be imposed: xxxx (3) By the mayor. if the respondent is an elective official of the Baranqay. (b) Preventive suspension may be imposed at any time after the issues are joined. when the evidence of guilt is stronq. and qiven the qravity of the offense. there is qreat probability that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and inteqrity of the records and other evidence: Provided, That, any single preventive suspension of local elective officials shall not extend beyond sixty (60) days: Provided, further, That in the event that several administrative cases are filed against an elective official, he cannot be preventively suspended for more than ninety (90) days within a single year on the same ground or grounds existing ang known at the time of the first suspension. (c) Upon expiration of the preventive suspension, the suspended elective official shall be deemed reinstated in office without prejudice to the continuation of the

proceedings against him, which shall be terminated within one hundred twenty (120) days from the time he was formally notified of the case against him. However, if the delay in the proceedings of the case is due to his fault, neglect, or request, other than the appeal duly filed, the duration of such delay shall not be counted in computing the time of termination of the case. (d) Any abuse of the exercise of the power of preventive suspension shall be penalized as abuse of authority." (Emphasis Supplied) b) Section 66, which governs the form and notice of decision rendered by the concerned disciplining authority "SECTION 66. Form and Notice of Decision. - (a) The investigation of the case shall be terminated within ninety (90) days from the start thereof. Within thirty (30) days after the end of the investigation, the Office of the President or the Sanggunian concerned shall render a decision in writing stating clearly and distinctly the facts and the reasons for such decision. Copies of said decision shall immediately be furnished the respondent and all interested parties. (b) The penalty of suspension shall not exceed the unexpired term of the respondent or a period of six (6) months for every administrative offense, nor shall said penalty be a bar to the candidacy of the respondent so suspended as long as he meets the qualifications required for the office. (c) The penalty of removal from office as a result of an administrative investigation shall be considered a bar to the candidacy of the respondent for any elective position. c) Section 67, which governs the filing of appeals to the decisions rendered by the concerned disciplining authority "SECTION 67. Administrative Appeals. - Decisions in administrative cases may, within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, be appealed to the following: (a) The Sangguniang Panlalawigan, in the case of decisions of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of component cities and the Sangguniang bayan; and (b) The Office of the President, in the case of decisions of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and the Sangguniang Panlungsod of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities. Decisions of the Office of the President shall be . final and executory." It can be inferred from the foregoing that a preventive suspension is imposed during the stage where investigation is still pending. This is implied from the afore-quoted provision which reads "there is great probability that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence". Accordingly, an order imposing preventive suspension against the respondent in an administrative case is not a final decision on the merits of the case or one that finally and completely disposes a case in an administrative complaint against an elective official. It is only interlocutory in character because it does not still put an end to the proceedings. The disciplining authority, after the imposition of preventive suspension, must still proceed to the hearing of the evidence to be presented by the other party in support of his claim or counterclaim. In

Sitchon vs. The Provincial SheriffofOccidental Negrosl, the Supreme Court explained the rationale on the rule that no appeal may be taken from an interlocutory order, thus: "The reason of the law in permitting appeal only from a final order or judgment, and not from interlocutory or incidental one, is to avoid multiplicity of appeals in a single action, which must necessarily suspend the hearing and decision on the merits of the case during the pendency of the appeal. If such appeal were allowed the trial on the merits of the case should necessarily be delayed for a considerable length of time, and compel the adverse party to incur unnecessary expenses; for one of the parties may interpose as many appeals as incidental questions may be raised by him and interlocutory orders rendered or issued by the lower court." Also, it may be well to stress that Section 67 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (which deals with administrative appeals) comes after Section 66 (which on the other hand deals with the termination of investigation and rendition of decision thereafter). In both Sections 66 and 67 of the Local Government Code of 1991 , the word "decision" was mentioned. The decision of the sangguniang bayan contemplated in Section 67 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991, which is the proper subject of the administrative appeals to the sangguniang panlalawigan, is one which renders the judgment on the merits in the case or one that finally and completely disposes a case in an administrative complaint against an elective official. Accordingly, the resolution or order of the Sangguniang Bayan placing Punong Barangay Cecile R. Villafuerte under preventive suspension cannot yet be appealed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and accordingly, the latter cannot order the stay of the preventive suspension order. Let us distinguish this however to the case of the Office of the President, which just like the Sangguniang Panlalawigan under Section 67 of the Local Government Code of 1991, has the appellate authority over decisions rendered by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. However, unlike the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, the Office of the President has issued Administrative Order No. 22, series of 2011 prescribing the rules and regulations governing appeals to the Office of the President. Hence, insofar as this appellate jurisdiction of the Office of the Office of the President is concerned over suspension orders against local elective officials, then Executive Secretary Salvador C. Medialdea issued a Memorandum dated December 1, 2022, pertinent portion of which reads: "With reference to the queries forwarded to the Office of the President (OP) on the above-referenced matter, and in order to guide the concerned authorities and the general public, please be advised on the following: 1. The timely filing before the OP of an appeal from decisions or orders issued by the Sanggunians in administrative cases against local elective officials shall not automatically stay the execution thereof, pursuant to Section 9 of Administrative Order (AO) No. 22, s. 2011, in relation to 1 G.R. No. 1--1853, 27 February 1948.

2. 3. Section 68 of the Local Government Code of 1991. The OP, however, has authority to order the stay of execution of the final decisions or orders of suspension from office issued by the Sanggunians against local elective officials, pursuant to Section 9 of AO No. 22 and consistent with the Supreme Court ruling in Berces Sr. v. Executive Secretary. The OP may likewise exercise appellate jurisdiction over orders of Sanqqunians imposinq preventive suspension against local elective officials. pursuant to Section I and 9 of AO No. 22. and the doctrine of exhaustion of administrative remedies. Moreover this is in aid of the appellate jurisdiction of the OP over decisions of such Sanqqunians in administrative cases." (Emphasis Supplied) In this Memorandum from the Office of the Executive Secretary, the OP has categorically declared that it has appellate jurisdiction over orders of the sanggunians imposing preventive suspension pursuant primarily to Sections 1 and 9 of its AO No. 22, series of 2011. A copy of said Memorandum from the Office of the Executive Secretary dated December 1, 2021 is hereto attached for ease of reference. As to the third issue, note that Section 63 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides a maximum number of days that an elective official may be preventively suspended pending investigation. Upon expiration thereof, said Section 63 further st?tes that the preventively suspension elective official is deemed reinstated, whether or not the investigation has been terminated. In Gloria vs. CA, et al.2, the Supreme Court explained the automatic lifting of the preventive suspension imposed upon the respondent upon expiration of the aforesaid maximum number of days that an elective official may be preventively suspended, thus: "Preventive suspension pending investigation is not a penalty. It is a measure intended to enable to enable the disciplining authority to investigate chargeé against respondent by preventing the latter from intimidating or any way influencing witnesses against him. If the investiqation is not finished and a decision is not rendered within that period. the suspension will be lifted and the respondent will automatically be reinstated. If after investigation respondent is found innocent of the charges and is exonerated, he should be reinstated." (Emphasis Supplied) The highlighted provision which states that "the suspension will be lifted and the respondent will automatically be reinstated" means by operation of law or that the respondent need not to take action before he is reinstated to office. However, it may be well to stress at this juncture that under Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 , preventive suspension is one of the causes of temporary incapacity of the incumbent local chief executive which paves the way to a temporary vacancy in his office. While it is true, as discussed earlier, that the preventively suspended elective official 2 G.R. No. 131012, 21 April 1999.

need not take action to be reinstated in office, in case of temporary •legal incapacities of local chief executives however such as herein Punong Barangay Villafuerte, Section 46 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991 requires that after said local chief executive has reported back to office, he shall submit to the appropriate sanggunian a written declaration of the fact that he has reported back to office and if such temporary incapacity is due to legal causes such as herein case of Punong Barangay Villafuerte, he shall also submit necessary documents showing that said legal causes no longer exist. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SE ARY: TOR R. LLAMAS ATTY J cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OU E JVRULLLs-LRALLD/c1p copy furnished: DIRECTOR PAISAL O.
